dod_intent_evidence: SBIR/STTR record: SOCOM Phase II ($1,298,434, 2023) 'Radio Location Tracker Mobile Mesh System,' whose own abstract states the objective is to build 'a field testable-prototype for in-field military use'; News section confirms a 2021 U.S. Navy NIWC Atlantic PNT prize predating the SBIR.
score_evidence: Commercial site leans on real deployed-customer proof points ('productivity has increased by 12 times... reached ROI in three months' — GE Aviation) rather than lab-demo bragging → lab_language_intensity scored low

SBIR abstract explicitly addresses GPS-denial: 'positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) for tagged objects, vehicles, or personnel without access to or sole reliance on military or commercial satellites... in GPS-occluded settings' → deployment_awareness_absence scored low

SBIR abstract: 'greatly enhance situational awareness for military operations, warfighters, and supply chain/support' names warfighters directly; commercial testimonials name real end users (gauge inspector, Site Digital Leader) → operator_absence scored low
no jobs data found in pack → hiring_profile_skew set to exactly 10 per rule
SOCOM Phase II awarded 2023 (~2-year period of performance typical) with company still 10-13 employees per channel notes 18 years after founding (2007) → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Commercial product offers 'On-Premises or Cloud Based Deployments' with only vague 'security needs' language, and no ATO/RMF/CMMC path is described for either option applied to the military PNT variant.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Getting the RRLT mesh's server software onto a government network for the SOCOM use case requires an accreditation story the commercial product page doesn't tell — 'meet your security needs' is not RMF/ATO language a program office can act on.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The deployment-flexibility messaging was built for industrial/commercial IT buyers, not adapted yet for the government-accreditation conversation the military variant will need.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: WISER has the flexibility to be deployed either on-premises or in the cloud providing flexibility to meet your security and deployment needs.

blind_spots.blind_spot: SBIR abstract promises 'secure textual communication for military users' over the mesh network but never mentions ITAR/export control handling or GFE integration with existing tactical radios/ATAK.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A comms capability riding alongside a PNT mesh is exactly the kind of feature that gets flagged for export control and needs explicit GFE/ATAK integration mechanics before a unit will trust it in the field — neither is addressed.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The Phase II effort is framed around extending existing RRLT positioning tech; the communications add-on reads as a late-stage feature addition without its own compliance/integration plan yet.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: it will offer limited and secure textual communication for military users connected via the wireless RRLT mesh network

blind_spots.blind_spot: Installation model is pitched as requiring 'no special training' with 'facility crews' managing setup — a commercial-facility assumption that doesn't survive an austere OCONUS deployment with no facility crew and no equivalent Ethernet/power infrastructure.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A unit fielding this in a GPS-occluded urban or underground environment doesn't have a 'facility crew' to daisy-chain antennas over Ethernet — sustainment, spares, and battery logistics for a tag fleet at scale aren't described anywhere.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The installation and support model was built and proven for industrial manufacturing floors (their core 18-year business), and hasn't yet been re-specified for tactical field deployment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: No special training is required and facility crews can generally manage the install.

opener_hook: WISER's SOCOM Phase II is adapting its industrial RTLS tech into a GPS-denied PNT mesh for warfighters — the accreditation path for the 'cloud based' deployment option isn't public yet.
what_they_do: Ultra-wideband real-time location system (RTLS) for industrial asset tracking, now adapting its GPS-denial-resilient positioning tech (RRLT) into a mobile mesh PNT system for military users under a SOCOM SBIR.
